assertions.summary: Node2 is Ubuntu 24.04.3 on a 6.8 kernel with predictable interface names and nftables-backed iptables.

evidence.command: uname -a; sed -n '1,12p' /etc/os-release; ip -br link; cat /proc/cmdline; readlink -f /etc/alternatives/iptables; iptables --version 2>&1
evidence.observation: Ubuntu 24.04.3 LTS; Linux 6.8.0-71-generic; interfaces enp1s0 and enp8s0; no net.ifnames=0 in the boot command line; iptables resolves to /usr/sbin/xtables-nft-multi and reports nf_tables.

assertions.summary: Both nodes resolve the canonical name only to node2's application-LAN address.

evidence.command: ip -4 -o addr show; ip route show table main
evidence.observation: Node1 eth0 is the default-route client interface at 10.100.160.10/24; eth1 is the separate application interface at 10.100.251.10/24.

evidence.command: getent ahostsv4 legacy-netapp.service.lan; getent ahostsv4 legacy-netapp.service.lan | awk '{print $1}' | sort -u
evidence.observation: Only 10.100.251.11 resolves.

evidence.command: getent ahostsv4 legacy-netapp.service.lan; getent ahostsv4 legacy-netapp.service.lan | awk '{print $1}' | sort -u; ip -4 -o addr show dev enp8s0
evidence.observation: Only 10.100.251.11 resolves, and enp8s0 owns 10.100.251.11/24.

assertions.summary: The correctly sourced node1 request returned the required health body.

evidence.command:
body=$(curl --interface eth1 --noproxy '*' --silent --show-error --max-time 5 --write-out '
HTTP_STATUS=%{http_code}' http://legacy-netapp.service.lan:4180/health); rc=$?; printf 'source_interface=eth1
curl_rc=%s
%s
' "$rc" "$body"; exit "$rc"
evidence.observation: curl_rc=0; response body was legacy-netapp-ok; HTTP_STATUS=200.

assertions.summary: The migrated identity endpoint returns migration-cohort-44.

evidence.command: curl --interface eth1 --noproxy '*' --silent --show-error --max-time 5 --write-out '\nHTTP_STATUS=%{http_code}\n' http://legacy-netapp.service.lan:4180/identity
evidence.observation: Response body was migration-cohort-44 and HTTP_STATUS=200.

assertions.summary: Both required service units are active and the port-4180 listeners bind only 10.100.251.11.

evidence.command: ss -H -ltnp 'sport = :4180'; systemctl show legacy-netapp@1.service -p ActiveState -p SubState -p MainPID -p User -p Group -p ExecStart; systemctl show legacy-netapp@2.service -p ActiveState -p SubState -p MainPID -p User -p Group -p ExecStart; ip -4 -o addr show
evidence.observation: Two listeners exist at 10.100.251.11:4180 with PIDs 1847 and 1848; both worker units are active/running; no wildcard, loopback, client-LAN, or IPv6 port-4180 bind appears.

assertions.summary: Both and only worker=1 and worker=2 served repeated requests through two SO_REUSEPORT processes.

evidence.command: w1=0; w2=0; other=0; errors=0; observed=''; for i in $(seq 1 32); do body=$(curl --interface eth1 --noproxy '*' --silent --show-error --fail --max-time 3 http://legacy-netapp.service.lan:4180/worker); rc=$?; if [ "$rc" -ne 0 ]; then errors=$((errors + 1)); continue; fi; observed="$observed $body"; case "$body" in worker=1) w1=$((w1 + 1));; worker=2) w2=$((w2 + 1));; *) other=$((other + 1));; esac; done; printf 'source_interface=eth1 requests=32 worker1=%s worker2=%s other=%s errors=%s\n' "$w1" "$w2" "$other" "$errors"; printf 'observed=%s\n' "$observed"; [ "$w1" -gt 0 ] && [ "$w2" -gt 0 ] && [ "$other" -eq 0 ] && [ "$errors" -eq 0]
evidence.observation: 32 successful requests: worker=1 appeared 20 times, worker=2 appeared 12 times, other=0, errors=0.

evidence.command: ss -H -ltnp 'sport = :4180'; grep -R -n -E 'SO_REUSEPORT|reuse_port|reuseport' /etc/systemd/system /usr/local /opt 2>/dev/null | head -20
evidence.observation: Distinct PIDs 1847 and 1848 share 10.100.251.11:4180; the running implementation contains listener.setsockopt(...SO_REUSEPORT..., 1). Both processes run as legacy-netapp with CapEff=0 and NoNewPrivs=1.
